column9: description
post prefill loop part 2
GEGLU on the NPU backend: FFN [up,gate,glu,down] in one split
GEGLU fused per 8-element tile cell into gate dequant: slower (per-cell call overhead, short vectors)
GEGLU fusion on gate via row buffer: never triggered (llama order is gate, up, GLU); build ~10% slower even with fusion off (codegen)
GEGLU fusion on up (triggers: +1.6% vs fusion off), still below #1 because of the inlined-code slowdown
fused GEGLU out of line (noinline): no change - slowdown was not inlining
fused collect as separate lambda: still slow with fusion off -> code layout (with -falign-*=64: #1 172.2, this 179.9)
GEGLU fused into up dequant (separate lambda) + pinned 64B function/loop alignment
RMS_NORM/ADD/MUL on NPU: slower - MUL by norm weight stays on CPU (weight buffer), so RMS_NORM on NPU adds a split boundary
supports_buft accepts host buffers: no scheduler copies of CPU-resident inputs (matmul guards weight buffer)
RMS_NORM/ADD/MUL on NPU with host buffers: still slower (sched keeps weight-owning MUL on CPU)
DC ZVA destination lines in dequant store path (no read-for-ownership)
DC ZVA on GEGLU output lines: slower (compute-bound loop)
NEON f32 binary ops in ggml-cpu: slower (already vectorized and/or layout shift in ggml-cpu)
pin 64B alignment in ggml-cpu: no gain
sign multiply + FWHT h=1,2 in one pass: no change - A-prep overlaps NPU runs, off the critical path
defer last dequant into next same-input matmul (gate->up): no gain - CPU dequant and NPU contend for DRAM bandwidth
RKNPU buffers advertised as host: CPU reads NPU outputs in place (no copy-back at splits)
Gemma-4 Q/K/V projections emitted back to back (one split): no gain
K-segmented weights (ffn_down) transform only their own Hadamard blocks
RMS_NORM/ADD/MUL on NPU re-tested without copies: still slower (separate passes vs ggml-cpu fused rms_norm_mul)
pipeline chunk 128 re-tested: slower (B re-reads compete for DRAM)
ffn_down K-segments merged into one pipelined pass (dequant2): fires (verified) but A/B 200.7/201.3 off vs 200.7/201.8 on — noise; the saved output RMW is small
dequant row blocks of 16 (sweep 4/8/16/32/64 = 200.8/190.9/187.8/191.5/187.9): 4 rows stays best, page-stride hypothesis wrong
FFN gate dequant deferred into up's fused GEGLU: gate FP32 never written/read back (microbench: N=10240 dequant ~3.5x slower/elem than N<=2560)
gate+up+GEGLU single tile pass (no row buffers): same-binary A/B +0.8% (205.5/205.7 off vs 207.3/206.7 on) but below keep threshold vs best
GEGLU divide -> recpe+2 Newton: slower (layout effect or FRECPS chain latency); not guarded
